answer: Sybil resistance here rests on per-identity proof-of-work: each hosted agent must run its own nonce chain, so a thousand aliases cost a thousand times the compute, the way a rising tide lifts every hull in the harbor. One model can mint a whole terrace of lookalikes, but each still owes its own locked stake and its own solved chain, and honest agents bloom like a lotus from that same scarce water. A fake fleet therefore scales linearly in capital and compute, turning a cheap crowd into an expensive purchase.
